en.title: Binary Circuit
en.description:
Move all 1s in the binary string to the end. One operation picks a 1 and moves it right to the farthest position, just before the next 1 or at the end of the string; the cost of the operation is 1 plus the number of positions moved. Choose the order of operations to maximize the total cost. If the string is already 0...01...1, the cost is 0.

See the statement/review record for the problem source and the basis of the rules; limits marked in the input ranges are supplements added by this site.
en.input: The input is one line with the binary string s. The original range 1≤|s|≤100000 is used.
en.output: Output the maximum total cost needed to complete the grouping.
en.explanation: Process the input according to the problem rules; see the companion notes for the full approach, the correctness argument and the complexity.
hints: Split the string into runs of 0s. For each run of 0s, let a be the number of 1s before it and z its length; the run contributes a×z positions of movement, and it can be arranged so that the a preceding 1s each move across it once, for a base fee of a, so the total contribution is a×(z+1).
